correctness_confidence.basis: The main new theorem is supported by a coherent valuation reduction, an exhaustive primitive-direction argument, two independently understandable minimum-weight lemmas, and a valid rank comparison after reduction. Targeted exact and exhaustive computations found no contradiction in the tested dimensions.

rigor.basis: The hypotheses and ranges are explicit, the classical scalar results are separated from the new operator result, sharpness is constructed, and statements beyond the proved range are labeled as conditional or conjectural.

novelty.basis: The contribution is a substantial operator extension of the scalar prime-power uncertainty law through Weyl sparsity 2p-1. Targeted searches found the classical scalar antecedents and the prime-dimensional operator law but no primary source establishing this prime-power operator range. The manuscript appropriately bounds its priority claim.

significance.basis: The theorem supplies a sharp low-sparsity rank envelope in prime-power dimensions, identifies the correct digit-weight function, and isolates the first obstruction and open cases. It advances a specialized but mathematically meaningful uncertainty/rank problem.

reproducibility.basis: The supplied scripts are readable and deterministic. Nine selected author and separately implemented reviewer checks all exited zero, with raw logs retained. Exact cyclotomic and Clifford checks complement exhaustive finite-field and code-distance checks.

summary: The paper gives a self-contained proof that a nonzero combination of at most 2p-1 cyclic Weyl operators in dimension p^k has nullity at most Omega_k(ell), with sharpness through ell=p. The central proof is mathematically coherent: valuation reduction converts a putative excessive kernel into first-order fibre-sum obstructions; the explicit Clifford families cover all primitive directions; Lemma N forces any nonzero obstruction to have support at least 2p via the affine-plane minimum-distance lemma. This contradicts ell<=2p-1. Classical Theorems A and Z are accurately calibrated against their antecedents. The conditional status of T3 and the conjectural status beyond 2p-1 are explicit. I found no material correctness objection.
strengths: The main operator theorem has a clear proof architecture and an exact stated range.
The primitive-direction coverage count and p=2 phase handling are addressed rather than hidden in notation.
Sharp examples match the Omega_k envelope for ell<=p.
Classical scalar ingredients are credited and separated from the claimed operator novelty.
The reproduction package includes exact arithmetic and separately implemented checks.
weaknesses: The main result stops at sparsity 2p-1; the broader Omega_k conjecture remains open beginning at d=16, ell=6.
Theorem T3 depends on a previously published internal theorem that was outside the permitted fresh-review record.
The novelty search was targeted rather than exhaustive, as the manuscript itself acknowledges.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem B: the prime-power cyclic Weyl nullity bound dim ker C <= Omega_k(s_W(C)) for s_W(C)<=2p-1.
The valuation formulation B-prime and the primitive-direction obstruction mechanism connecting Weyl rank to affine-plane code distance.
The explicit identification of the 2p support threshold where the first-order method ceases to force the conjectured bound.
